title: Inconsistent Read Phantoms under Weak Isolation
pattern: Running data migration or audit logic that executes range reads or aggregations under read-committed or snapshot isolation levels without serializable isolation.
why_bad: Concurrent transactions can insert or delete rows during execution. The reader will see a "phantom" state where some changes are partially reflected, leading to invalid calculations or corrupt database migration records [410, 809, 814].
detection: Multiple sequential SQL aggregation/range queries executed over the same table inside a single migration transaction when the isolation level is set to anything weaker than `Serializable`.
counterexample: Valid if the table is locked exclusively against writes or if the application is running in an offline maintenance window. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Execute critical migrations requiring absolute consistency under `Serializable` isolation, or explicitly lock the affected rows using `SELECT FOR UPDATE` [205, 410, 813].
source: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, "Concurrency" [410, 809, 810, 813, 814]; Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 7 [205]
